newsitem.title: USA: Boeing and McDonnell in collaboration pact.
newsitem.headline: Boeing and McDonnell in collaboration pact.

text.p: Boeing Co. and McDonnell Douglas Corp. reached an agreement Tuesday to collaborate on future Boeing wide-body commercial airplane programmes.
In a joint statement, the aerospace companies said the first project McDonnell Douglas will participate in is the development of proposed new versions of the Boeing 747 jumbo jet.
The move comes as Boeing faces record orders for its commercial aircraft and McDonnell Douglas is looking for ways to keep its employees working.

McDonnell Douglas recently lost a bid to build a next-generation fighter plane for the Pentagon and has shelved plans to build a long-range commercial aircraft that would go head-to-head with the 747.

"We have a record number of orders for commercial jets and several ongoing development programmes," said Ron Woodard, president of Boeing Commercial Airplane Group. "McDonnell Douglas has excellent design and production capability -- both in people and facilities -- that are not being fully utilized.
"We look forward to applying those resources to future Boeing wide-body airplane programmes in a way that is a win-win for both of us."

Boeing said initially the agreement is expected to bring several hundred McDonnell Douglas employees to Seattle in January to begin assisting with engineering design and analysis on the 747-500X/-600X.
The agreement should be finalised in January.
McDonnell's stock gained 75 cents to $53.375 and Boeing added 50 cents to $98 in late morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
